#### `HeaderSource`

```ts
type HeaderSource =
  | Readonly<Record<string, string>>
  | ((req: HttpRequest) => Readonly<Record<string, string>> | undefined);
```

Headers as data, or computed when each request runs (e.g. read a CSRF `<meta>`).

#### `HttpDriverOptions`

```ts
interface HttpDriverOptions {
  /** Driver name used for substitution (`el.drivers`). Default `'http'`. */
  readonly name?: string;
  /**
   * Default headers for every request through this driver: app-level concerns such as a CSRF
   * token or an API key, so components and stores never read the DOM themselves. This is the
   * one place a CSRF token is configured (ADR 0022). Per-request `headers` win over these.
   *
   *   provideDrivers(document.body, { http: makeHttpDriver({ headers: csrfFromMeta('csrf-token') }) });
   */
  readonly headers?: HeaderSource;
  /** Resolves relative URLs. Default: the document location. */
  readonly baseUrl?: string;
  readonly fetch?: typeof fetch;
  readonly concurrency?: Concurrency;
  /**
   * Aborts a request that takes longer than this, failing with `HttpTimeoutError`. Applies per
   * attempt: under `retry(…)` each attempt gets the full time. Default: no limit.
   */
  readonly timeoutMs?: number;
  // No retry option: wrap the driver instead, `retry(makeHttpDriver(…), policy)` (ADR 0022).
}
```


#### `HttpError`

```ts
type HttpError =
  | {
      readonly _tag: 'HttpStatusError';
      readonly url: string;
      readonly status: number;
      readonly statusText: string;
      /** The response body: parsed JSON, or text, or `undefined` when empty. */
      readonly body: unknown;
      /** `body` decoded by the request's `errorSchema`, when it was given and matched. */
      readonly detail?: unknown;
    }
  | { readonly _tag: 'HttpNetworkError'; readonly url: string; readonly message: string }
  /** The attempt took longer than the driver's `timeoutMs`. */
  | { readonly _tag: 'HttpTimeoutError'; readonly url: string; readonly timeoutMs: number }
  | {
      readonly _tag: 'HttpDecodeError';
      readonly url: string;
      readonly issues: ReadonlyArray<StandardSchemaV1.Issue>;
    };
```

Every way a request can fail. Delivered to `onFailure`, never thrown into the view.

#### `HttpMethod`

```ts
type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE';
```


#### `HttpRequest`

```ts
interface HttpRequest {
  readonly url: string;
  readonly method?: HttpMethod;
  readonly headers?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  /** Sent as JSON, except `FormData` and `URLSearchParams`, which are sent as forms. */
  readonly body?: unknown;
  /** Decodes the JSON response. Any Standard Schema library works (Zod, Valibot, Effect…). */
  readonly schema?: StandardSchemaV1;
  /**
   * Decodes the body of a non-2xx response into `HttpStatusError.detail` (for example a 422
   * `IntentRejected`). A body that doesn't match leaves `detail` unset; `body` is always kept.
   */
  readonly errorSchema?: StandardSchemaV1;
}
```

An HTTP request described as data.

#### `RequestHandlers`

```ts
interface RequestHandlers<O, MS, MF> {
  /** Decodes the response; its output type becomes `onSuccess`'s input. */
  readonly schema?: StandardSchemaV1<unknown, O>;
  /** Decodes non-2xx bodies into `HttpStatusError.detail` (e.g. a 422 `IntentRejected`). */
  readonly errorSchema?: StandardSchemaV1;
  readonly onSuccess: (body: O) => MS | undefined;
  readonly onFailure?: (error: HttpError) => MF | undefined;
  /** Concurrency lane, e.g. `'search'`. Default `'http'`. */
  readonly key?: string;
  readonly concurrency?: Concurrency;
}
```


#### `SubmitFormOptions`

```ts
interface SubmitFormOptions<MS, MF> {
  readonly method?: 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'PATCH';
  /**
   * A CSRF token the app already holds, for this submission only. The header defaults to
   * `x-csrf-token`. A token from a `<meta>` is configured once, on the driver:
   * `makeHttpDriver({ headers: csrfFromMeta('csrf-token') })` (ADR 0022).
   */
  readonly csrf?: { readonly token: string; readonly header?: string };
  /** The server's success answer, e.g. `{ _tag: 'Redirected', location }` (see `redirectedTo`). */
  readonly onSuccess: (body: unknown) => MS | undefined;
  /** Any failure except a 422 `IntentRejected`, which goes to the `IntentRejected` reducer. */
  readonly onFailure?: (error: HttpError) => MF | undefined;
  /** Concurrency lane. Default `form:<url>`. */
  readonly key?: string;
  /** Default `exhaust`: a second submit while one is in flight is ignored. */
  readonly concurrency?: Concurrency;
}
```

## `@gyral/http/testing`

### Functions

| [`fakeHttp`](#http-testing-fakehttp) | `el.drivers = { http: fakeHttp() }` (or `provideDrivers(root, { http })`), then `http.respondNext({ body })` or `http.reply(422, problem)`. |

#### `fakeHttp`

```ts
function fakeHttp(options: FakeHttpOptions = {}): FakeHttp
```

`el.drivers = { http: fakeHttp() }` (or `provideDrivers(root, { http })`), then
`http.respondNext({ body })` or `http.reply(422, problem)`. Request inputs are recorded in
`requests` (alias `inputs`).

```ts
class FakeHttpResponderError extends Error {

    readonly request: HttpRequest,
    cause: unknown,
  );
}
```

### Types and interfaces

You rarely write most of these yourself: TypeScript infers them from the functions above. Look one up when an example or a compiler error names it.

| Name | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`FakeHttp`](#http-testing-fakehttp) |  |
| [`FakeHttpCall`](#http-testing-fakehttpcall) | One request the fake driver received. |
| [`FakeHttpOptions`](#http-testing-fakehttpoptions) |  |
| [`FakeResponse`](#http-testing-fakeresponse) | What a fake server answers: a status (default 200) and a JSON body (omit for none). |

#### `FakeHttp`

```ts
interface FakeHttp extends Driver<HttpRequest, unknown, HttpError> {
  readonly calls: readonly FakeHttpCall[];
  /** Every request so far. */
  readonly requests: readonly HttpRequest[];
  /** Same as `requests`; matches `fakeDriver(…).inputs` from `@gyral/testing`. */
  readonly inputs: readonly HttpRequest[];
  /** Errors thrown (or rejected) by the `respond` option, in order. */
  readonly responderErrors: readonly unknown[];
  /** Answers the oldest request that is still waiting. Throws if there is none. */
  respondNext(response?: FakeResponse): void;
  /** Shorthand for `respondNext({ status, body })`, e.g. `reply(422, problem)`. */
  reply(status: number, body?: unknown): void;
  /** Fails the oldest waiting request as a network error. Throws if there is none. */
  failNext(message?: string): void;
}
```


#### `FakeHttpCall`

```ts
interface FakeHttpCall {
  readonly request: HttpRequest;
  readonly signal: AbortSignal;
  readonly settled: boolean;
  /** Answers this request; the real driver then decodes it. */
  readonly respond: (response?: FakeResponse) => void;
  /** Fails this request as a network error (`HttpNetworkError`). */
  readonly fail: (message?: string) => void;
}
```

One request the fake driver received.

#### `FakeHttpOptions`

```ts
interface FakeHttpOptions {
  /** Driver name to substitute (`el.drivers`, providers). Default `'http'`. */
  readonly name?: string;
  /** Answer every request immediately. Without it, requests wait for `respondNext`. */
  readonly respond?: (request: HttpRequest) => FakeResponse | Promise<FakeResponse>;
  /** Base URL for relative request URLs. Default `'http://localhost/'`. */
  readonly baseUrl?: string;
  readonly headers?: HeaderSource;
  readonly concurrency?: Concurrency;
  /**
   * Called when the `respond` option throws or rejects. That is a bug in the test, not a
   * network failure, so by default it is rethrown as an uncaught error (Vitest fails the run).
   * The request itself still fails (as `HttpNetworkError`) so the component never hangs.
   */
  readonly onResponderError?: (error: unknown, request: HttpRequest) => void;
}
```


#### `FakeResponse`

```ts
interface FakeResponse {
  readonly status?: number;
  readonly statusText?: string;
  readonly body?: unknown;
}
```

What a fake server answers: a status (default 200) and a JSON body (omit for none).

# @gyral/router

> Gyral router: typed route tables, navigation as commands, History API baseline with Navigation API enhancement.

Source: https://gyral.dev/docs/api/router/

Gyral router: typed route tables, navigation as commands, History API baseline with Navigation API enhancement.

```sh
npm install @gyral/router @gyral/core
```

> **Writing code? Start from working code, not from this page.** [Routing](https://gyral.dev/docs/routing/). Adapt the closest example and check it, then look a name up here when you are about to call it.

Generated from the package's type declarations. Entry points: [`@gyral/router`](#gyralrouter).

## `@gyral/router`

### Functions

| Name | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`listen`](#router-listen) | Streams the current location, then every URL change, as messages until the component disconnects (a streaming command, ADR 0006/0009). |
| [`makeRouter`](#router-makerouter) | A router driver. |
| [`navigate`](#router-navigate) | Navigates in-app (pushes a history entry, or replaces the current one). |
| [`routes`](#router-routes) |  |
| [`setHead`](#router-sethead) | Makes the document's head this `Head` (ADR 0019): the title, `lang`/`dir`, and every managed element (description, robots, canonical, meta, links, JSON-LD). |

#### `listen`

```ts
function listen<M>(toMsg: (location: RouteLocation) => M | undefined): Command<M>
```

Streams the current location, then every URL change, as messages until the component
disconnects (a streaming command, ADR 0006/0009). Start it from `subscriptions`, which restarts
it when a moved or re-attached component connects again (a command from `init` is not):


```ts
subscriptions: () => [listen((location) => ({ _tag: 'Routed', location }))]
```


#### `makeRouter`

```ts
function makeRouter(options: RouterOptions = {}): RouterDriver
```

A router driver. Listeners are installed on first use, never at import time.

#### `navigate`

```ts
function navigate(url: string, options: NavigateOptions = {}): Command<never>
```

Navigates in-app (pushes a history entry, or replaces the current one). In the browser, once
the new page has rendered, a push scrolls to the `#fragment` target or the top and resets
focus, as the browser does for a page load (ADR 0009 "Scroll and focus"); `scroll: false` or
`focusReset: false` leaves that to the app. A `replace` (keeping the query in sync with a
search box) leaves scroll and focus alone unless `scroll: true` / `focusReset: true`.

#### `routes`

```ts
function routes<const T extends RouteTable>(
  table: T,
  options: { readonly matcher?: Matcher } = {},
): Routes<T>
```


#### `setHead`

```ts
function setHead(head: Head): Command<never>
```

Makes the document's head this `Head` (ADR 0019): the title, `lang`/`dir`, and every managed
element (description, robots, canonical, meta, links, JSON-LD). Managed elements the new head
doesn't name are removed; unchanged ones are not written; content from `renderPage({ extraHead })`
is never touched. The memory history records it instead. Build the head with one pure
function and pass the same function's result to the server's `renderPage()`:


```ts
Routed: (s, m) => [next, [setHead(pageHead(site.match(m.location.href), origin))]]
```


### Constants

| Name | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`router`](#router-router) | The default router (global window, Navigation API when available). |

#### `router`

```ts
const router: RouterDriver
```

The default router (global window, Navigation API when available).

#### `AfterNavigation`

```ts
interface AfterNavigation {
  /** Scroll to the `#fragment` target or the top (push), or restore (back/forward). */
  readonly scroll: boolean;
  /** Move focus to the first `[autofocus]` element, or reset it to the page start. */
  readonly focusReset: boolean;
}
```

What the browser history does once a navigation's render has committed (ADR 0009).

#### `LocationLike`

```ts
type LocationLike = Pick<Location, 'href' | 'origin' | 'pathname' | 'search'>;
```

What link capture and URL resolution need from a location (a `URL` qualifies).

#### `Matcher`

```ts
type Matcher = 'auto' | 'urlpattern' | 'fallback';
```


#### `MemoryOptions`

```ts
interface MemoryOptions {
  /** Starting URL, absolute or relative to `origin`. Default `'/'`. */
  readonly initial?: string;
  /** Origin that relative URLs resolve against. Default `'http://localhost'`. */
  readonly origin?: string;
  /**
   * Intercept same-origin link clicks. **Default `false`** (opt in): a router that captures
   * every link on the page breaks multi-page apps where only one component routes (ADR 0009).
   */
  readonly captureLinks?: boolean;
  /**
   * Where to capture link clicks when `captureLinks` is on. Default: the (global, or the
   * browser history's) `document`. Passing an element also turns capture on and limits it to
   * that subtree; `null` turns it off. Capture is only active while a component listens.
   */
  readonly linkRoot?: EventTarget | null;
}
```


#### `NavigateOptions`

```ts
interface NavigateOptions extends Partial<AfterNavigation> {
  /** Replace the current history entry instead of pushing one. Default `false`. */
  readonly replace?: boolean;
}
```

Options of `navigate()`.

#### `Params`

```ts
type Params<Path extends string> = Path extends `${infer Head}/${infer Rest}`
  ? Param<Head> & Params<Rest>
  : Param<Path>;
```

Named required strings, optional strings and trailing catch-all arrays, inferred by path.

#### `RouteLocation`

```ts
interface RouteLocation {
  readonly href: string;
  readonly pathname: string;
  readonly search: string;
  readonly hash: string;
  /** Increases on every URL change seen by this router. */
  readonly seq: number;
}
```

The document location, numbered in the order this router saw changes.

#### `RouteMatch`

```ts
type RouteMatch<T extends RouteTable> = {
  [N in keyof T & string]: {
    readonly name: N;
    readonly params: Params<T[N]>;
    readonly path: string;
  };
}[keyof T & string];
```

The route name discriminates its params. `path` is the canonical href for those captures.

#### `RouterDriver`

```ts
interface RouterDriver extends Driver<RouterInput, RouteLocation | undefined> {
  /** The current URL and last head as this router sees them. */
  readonly snapshot: () => RouterSnapshot;
  /** Removes document listeners and ends running `listen` commands. */
  readonly dispose: () => void;
}
```


#### `RouterInput`

```ts
type RouterInput =
  | ({
      readonly _tag: 'Navigate';
      readonly url: string;
      readonly replace: boolean;
    } & Partial<AfterNavigation>)
  | { readonly _tag: 'Traverse'; readonly delta: number }
  | { readonly _tag: 'Head'; readonly head: Head }
  | { readonly _tag: 'Listen' };
```


#### `RouterOptions`

```ts
interface RouterOptions extends MemoryOptions {
  /** Driver name used for substitution (`el.drivers`). Default `'router'`. */
  readonly name?: string;
  /**
   * `'browser'` (default) drives the real document. `'memory'` keeps entries in memory: no
   * global URL changes, no `window` needed (tests, servers). See `initial` and `origin`.
   * `captureLinks`/`linkRoot` apply to both histories.
   */
  readonly history?: 'browser' | 'memory';
  /** Browser history: default the global window, resolved on first use (safe on a server). */
  readonly window?: Window;
  /** Browser history: use the Navigation API when present. Default `true`. */
  readonly navigationApi?: boolean;
  /**
   * Browser history, once a navigation has rendered: scroll to the `#fragment` target or the
   * top (push) and restore the position on back/forward. Default `true`; `false` for apps that
   * manage scroll themselves. A replace never scrolls unless `navigate(url, { scroll: true })`;
   * `navigate(url, { scroll })` overrides it per call.
   */
  readonly scroll?: boolean;
  /**
   * Browser history, once a navigation has rendered: move focus to the first `[autofocus]`
   * element, or reset it to the page start, unless something took focus during the navigation
   * (a `focus('main h1')` command). Default `true` (a replace: only with `focusReset: true`).
   * `navigate(url, { focusReset })` per call.
   */
  readonly focusReset?: boolean;
}
```


#### `RouterSnapshot`

```ts
interface RouterSnapshot {
  readonly href: string;
  /** The last `setHead()` head, if any (the browser applies it to the document too). */
  readonly head: Head | undefined;
  /** Number of history entries (memory history; `history.length` in a browser). */
  readonly length: number;
}
```

The router's current URL and last head, for tests and server-side assertions.

#### `Routes`

```ts
interface Routes<T extends RouteTable> {
  readonly table: T;
  /** First route in table order matching the pathname. A string beginning with / is a path. */
  match(url: string | URL): RouteMatch<T> | undefined;
  /** Percent-encode each parameter or catch-all segment; omit absent optional parameters. */
  href<N extends keyof T & string>(name: N, params: Params<T[N]>): string;
}
```


#### `RouteTable`

```ts
type RouteTable = Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
```

# @gyral/time

> Gyral time: delays, debounces and wall-clock ticks (every) as commands.

Source: https://gyral.dev/docs/api/time/

Gyral time: delays, debounces and wall-clock ticks (every) as commands.

```sh
npm install @gyral/time @gyral/core
```

> **Writing code? Start from working code, not from this page.** [Effects and drivers](https://gyral.dev/docs/effects/). Adapt the closest example and check it, then look a name up here when you are about to call it.

Generated from the package's type declarations. Entry points: [`@gyral/time`](#gyraltime).

## `@gyral/time`

### Functions

| Name | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`debounce`](#time-debounce) | Sends `msg` once `ms` pass without another `debounce` in the same lane: a delay under `switch`, so each call cancels the pending one. |
| [`delay`](#time-delay) | Sends `msg` after `ms`. |
| [`every`](#time-every) | Sends `toMsg(now)` at once and then every `ms`, `now` being `Date.now()` (virtual under `virtualTime()`), until it is stopped. |

#### `debounce`

```ts
function debounce<M>(ms: number, msg: M, key = 'time:debounce'): Command<M>
```

Sends `msg` once `ms` pass without another `debounce` in the same lane: a delay under
`switch`, so each call cancels the pending one.

#### `delay`

```ts
function delay<M>(ms: number, msg: M, lane: Lane = {}): Command<M>
```

Sends `msg` after `ms`. By default every delay runs (`merge` in lane `time:delay`).

#### `every`

```ts
function every<M>(
  ms: number,
  toMsg: (now: number) => M | undefined,
  key = 'time:every',
): Command<M>
```

Sends `toMsg(now)` at once and then every `ms`, `now` being `Date.now()` (virtual under
`virtualTime()`), until it is stopped. Made for `subscriptions` (ADR 0025):
`subscriptions: (s) => (s.live ? [every(1000, (now) => ({ _tag: 'Tick', now }))] : [])`.
Each `every` runs in lane `key` (`switch`: another one in the same lane replaces it).

# @gyral/ssr

> Gyral server rendering: Declarative Shadow DOM pages with hydration seeds.

Source: https://gyral.dev/docs/api/ssr/

Gyral server rendering: Declarative Shadow DOM pages with hydration seeds.

```sh
npm install @gyral/ssr @gyral/core
```

> **Writing code? Start from working code, not from this page.** [Server rendering](https://gyral.dev/docs/server-rendering/). Adapt the closest example and check it, then look a name up here when you are about to call it.

Generated from the package's type declarations. Entry points: [`@gyral/ssr`](#gyralssr), [`@gyral/ssr/static`](#gyralssrstatic), [`@gyral/ssr/node`](#gyralssrnode).

## `@gyral/ssr`

### Functions

| Name | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`contentSecurityPolicy`](#ssr-contentsecuritypolicy) | A `Content-Security-Policy` header value whose `style-src` allows Gyral's `<style>` elements by hash, for the components registered when it is called (import them first). |
| [`formAction`](#ssr-formaction) | A request handler for a `<form method="post">` that works with JavaScript disabled, and answers the JS path (`submitForm` in `@gyral/http`, `Accept: application/json`) with JSON: valid → the handler's response, a redirect turned into `{ _tag: 'Redirected', location }`; invalid → `422` with the `IntentRejected` (without `values`). |
| [`rejectWith`](#ssr-rejectwith) | Rejects a submission that passed the schema but failed a server-only check (email taken, wrong password). |
| [`renderPage`](#ssr-renderpage) | An HTML `Response` for a full page, its body pulled in chunks from a synchronous render (one component boundary per pull): load data first, since nothing is awaited and there is no async or suspense streaming. |
| [`renderToString`](#ssr-rendertostring) | Renders to a complete string (tests, caching, static generation), with this request's stores in scope (ADR 0013). |
| [`seeOther`](#ssr-seeother) | 303 See Other: the redirect that turns a POST into a GET (no resubmit on reload). |
| [`styleHashes`](#ssr-stylehashes) | `'sha256-…'` hashes of every registered shadow component's declarative-shadow-root `<style>`, for a `Content-Security-Policy` `style-src`. |
| [`wantsJson`](#ssr-wantsjson) | Whether the request asks for JSON rather than a page (`Accept: application/json` without `text/html`): `submitForm` and other fetch calls do, a browser's form post doesn't. |

#### `contentSecurityPolicy`

```ts
function contentSecurityPolicy(options: CspOptions = {}): Promise<string>
```

A `Content-Security-Policy` header value whose `style-src` allows Gyral's `<style>`
elements by hash, for the components registered when it is called (import them first).
`renderPage({ …, csp: options })` builds it at render time instead; pass this result to
`renderPage({ …, csp })` or set it on any response. Other inline styles (`style`
attributes, hand-written `<style>` in `head`) are not covered.

#### `formAction`

```ts
function formAction<Schema extends StandardSchemaV1>(
  definition: FormDefinition<Schema>,
  handlers: FormActionHandlers<StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput<Schema>>,
): (request: Request) => Promise<Response>
```

A request handler for a `<form method="post">` that works with JavaScript disabled, and
answers the JS path (`submitForm` in `@gyral/http`, `Accept: application/json`) with JSON:
valid → the handler's response, a redirect turned into `{ _tag: 'Redirected', location }`;
invalid → `422` with the `IntentRejected` (without `values`). On the no-JS path `values`
never includes the definition's secret fields (`defineForm(schema, { secret })`).

#### `rejectWith`

```ts
function rejectWith(issues: string | readonly FieldIssue[]): FormReject
```

Rejects a submission that passed the schema but failed a server-only check (email taken,
wrong password). A string is a form-level message (path `''`). `formAction` turns it into
the same `IntentRejected` as a schema failure, on both the no-JS and the JS path.

#### `renderPage`

```ts
function renderPage(options: PageOptions, init: ResponseInit = {}): Response
```

An HTML `Response` for a full page, its body pulled in chunks from a synchronous render (one
component boundary per pull): load data first, since nothing is awaited
and there is no async or suspense streaming. Status and headers are final before the first
byte. `csp` sets the `Content-Security-Policy`
header: a string as is, or `contentSecurityPolicy()`'s options to build it now, with every
component registered by the time the page renders (and the page's `styles`). With
`csp: { styleAttributes: 'hash' }` the page is rendered to a string first, so the header can
list its `style` attribute values by hash (ADR 0020); a render error then throws here.
A component whose `init` or view throws renders its error view and the page goes on;
`onError` hears it, and `onError: 'throw'` renders to a string first and throws here instead,
before any byte is sent (ADR 0024).

#### `renderToString`

```ts
function renderToString(value: ChildValue, options: RenderOptions = {}): Promise<string>
```

Renders to a complete string (tests, caching, static generation), with this request's stores
in scope (ADR 0013).

#### `seeOther`

```ts
function seeOther(location: string): Response
```

303 See Other: the redirect that turns a POST into a GET (no resubmit on reload).

#### `styleHashes`

```ts
function styleHashes(): Promise<readonly string[]>
```

`'sha256-…'` hashes of every registered shadow component's declarative-shadow-root `<style>`,
for a `Content-Security-Policy` `style-src`.

#### `wantsJson`

```ts
const wantsJson: (request: Request) => boolean
```

Whether the request asks for JSON rather than a page (`Accept: application/json` without
`text/html`): `submitForm` and other fetch calls do, a browser's form post doesn't. The rule
`formAction` answers by; for your own routes that serve both.

### Types and interfaces

You rarely write most of these yourself: TypeScript infers them from the functions above. Look one up when an example or a compiler error names it.

| Name | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`ComponentAssets`](#ssr-componentassets) | The client side of automatic component loading, for `renderPage({ components })`: from `componentsFromManifest()` in production, handed over by `productionServer` and `gyralDevServer`. |
| [`ComponentModule`](#ssr-componentmodule) | One component's client module: what to preload and link when the page renders its tag. |
| [`CspDirectives`](#ssr-cspdirectives) | CSP directives by name: a source list, as one string or a list of sources. |
| [`CspOptions`](#ssr-cspoptions) |  |
| [`FormActionHandlers`](#ssr-formactionhandlers) |  |
| [`FormReject`](#ssr-formreject) | A server-side rejection of a schema-valid submission (see `rejectWith`). |
| [`PageOptions`](#ssr-pageoptions) | The page shell's options. |
| [`RenderOptions`](#ssr-renderoptions) |  |

#### `ComponentAssets`

```ts
interface ComponentAssets {
  /** URL of the loader module, which imports each rendered tag's module when it's in the page. */
  readonly loader: string;
  /** Tag → its client module. A rendered tag missing here won't hydrate (development warns). */
  readonly modules: ReadonlyMap<string, ComponentModule>;
  /** The loader's own imports, preloaded with it (production). */
  readonly preload?: readonly string[];
  /** More module scripts for pages with components (development: Vite's client). */
  readonly scripts?: readonly string[];
}
```

The client side of automatic component loading, for `renderPage({ components })`: from
`componentsFromManifest()` in production, handed over by `productionServer` and
`gyralDevServer`.

#### `ComponentModule`

```ts
interface ComponentModule {
  /** The module's chunk and its static imports (production; empty in development). */
  readonly preload: readonly string[];
  /** Hashed CSS the module imports (production; empty in development). */
  readonly stylesheets: readonly string[];
}
```

One component's client module: what to preload and link when the page renders its tag.

#### `CspDirectives`

```ts
type CspDirectives = Readonly<Record<string, string | readonly string[]>>;
```

CSP directives by name: a source list, as one string or a list of sources.

#### `CspOptions`

```ts
interface CspOptions {
  /**
   * Precomputed component `<style>` hashes from `styleHashes()` at build time. Append them
   * to registered component hashes, allowing a policy-only server to read JSON metadata
   * without executing every component module. Regenerate with each release's actual CSS.
   */
  readonly componentStyleHashes?: readonly string[];
  /**
   * Your other directives (`default-src`, `script-src`, …). A `style-src` given here is kept
   * and the hashes are appended; without one it is `'self'` plus the hashes.
   */
  readonly directives?: CspDirectives;
  /**
   * The page's global styles, exactly as passed to `renderPage({ styles })`, hashed too. In
   * `renderPage({ csp })` it defaults to the page's own `styles`.
   */
  readonly styles?: string | readonly string[];
  /**
   * The page's inline head scripts, exactly as passed to `renderPage({ headScripts })`, allowed in
   * `script-src` by hash (a `script-src` given in `directives` is kept and the hashes appended;
   * without one it is `'self'` plus the hashes). In `renderPage({ csp })` it defaults to the
   * page's own `headScripts`.
   */
  readonly scripts?: string | readonly string[];
  /**
   * `'hash'` (`renderPage` only, ADR 0020): allow the `style` attributes the page writes by
   * hash, in `style-src-attr` with `'unsafe-hashes'`, so they apply on first paint under a
   * strict policy. The page is rendered to a string before the response is built (its
   * headers need every value), so the body isn't chunked. Covers static, bound, multi-part and
   * element-hook values, not `raw()` markup. A `style-src-attr` given in `directives` is kept;
   * when it allows `'unsafe-inline'`, no hashes are added (a hash would disable it).
   */
  readonly styleAttributes?: 'hash';
  /**
   * The most `style` attribute hashes one page's header lists (default 128, about 7 KB of
   * header; proxies reject large headers). Values past it are left out and logged once;
   * hydration applies them.
   */
  readonly maxStyleHashes?: number;
}
```


#### `FormActionHandlers`

```ts
interface FormActionHandlers<T> {
  /**
   * The form's `data-intent` name. It becomes `IntentRejected.intent`, exactly as on the
   * JS path, so the component's reducer can't tell the two apart.
   */
  readonly intent: string;
  /**
   * Valid submission: do the work, then usually `seeOther(url)` (Post/Redirect/Get), or return
   * `rejectWith(…)` when a server-only check fails.
   */
  readonly valid: (
    data: T,
    request: Request,
  ) => Response | FormReject | Promise<Response | FormReject>;
  /**
   * Invalid submission without JavaScript: re-render the page with the component's
   * `.initialMessages` set to `[rejected]`, typically with status 422. The component's own
   * `IntentRejected` reducer turns it into state, so the errors render through the same view as
   * with JavaScript. Leave it out for an endpoint only `submitForm` calls: every rejection is
   * then the JSON 422.
   */
  readonly invalid?: (rejected: IntentRejected, request: Request) => Response | Promise<Response>;
}
```


#### `FormReject`

```ts
interface FormReject {
  readonly _tag: 'FormReject';
  readonly issues: readonly FieldIssue[];
}
```

A server-side rejection of a schema-valid submission (see `rejectWith`).

#### `PageOptions`

```ts
interface PageOptions extends RenderOptions, Head {
  /** The hydratable app: an `html` template, usually one custom element. */
  readonly body: ChildValue;
  /**
   * Server-only head content the head model doesn't cover, written with `html` (icons that
   * never change, preconnect hints, …). Never touched by `setHead()`.
   */
  readonly extraHead?: ChildValue;
  /**
   * Global CSS for the document (your app's own stylesheet text, e.g. a `?raw` import), written
   * as `<style>` elements in the head. A `</style` inside the text is escaped, so it can't
   * close the element early. Trusted CSS only: never put user input here.
   */
  readonly styles?: string | readonly string[];
  /**
   * Stylesheet URLs, written as `<link rel="stylesheet">` before `styles`: in production,
   * `clientAssetsFromManifest()`'s `css` (the hashed CSS Vite emitted for what the client entry
   * imports), served immutable and allowed by `style-src 'self'` without hashes.
   */
  readonly stylesheets?: readonly string[];
  /** Module scripts to load, e.g. the client entry. */
  readonly scripts?: readonly string[];
  /**
   * Inline classic scripts written early in the head, after the managed head entries and
   * before any stylesheet, so they run before the page paints (a theme script that sets
   * `data-theme` from storage, say). Trusted code only. A `</script` inside the text is escaped.
   * `renderPage({ csp })` allows them in `script-src` by hash.
   */
  readonly headScripts?: string | readonly string[];
  /**
   * Modules to fetch early with `<link rel="modulepreload">`, written before `scripts`: in
   * production, `clientAssetsFromManifest()`'s `modulepreload` (the entry's static imports and
   * the hydration chunk), so hydration doesn't wait for extra round trips.
   */
  readonly modulepreload?: readonly string[];
  /**
   * `renderPage` only: the `Content-Security-Policy` header. Pass `contentSecurityPolicy()`'s
   * options (`{ directives }`; the page's `styles` are included) to build it when the page
   * renders, with every component registered by then and the `<style>` elements allowed by
   * hash; or a header value, e.g. from `await contentSecurityPolicy({ styles })` (development
   * warns when it lacks a registered component's hash).
   */
  readonly csp?: string | CspOptions;
}
```

The page shell's options. The `Head` fields (title, description, canonical, robots, meta,
links, JSON-LD, lang, dir) are the managed head (ADR 0019): the same object a client router
applies with `setHead()` after a navigation, so build both from one function.

#### `RenderOptions`

```ts
interface RenderOptions {
  /**
   * This request's store instances (ADR 0013). Components read them during the render; a
   * store not listed starts from its `init`. Create new instances per request.
   */
  readonly stores?: readonly AnyStoreInstance[];
  /**
   * Development markers and checks. Default: on when
   * `@gyral/core` resolves with the `development` condition (Vite's dev server, Vitest).
   */
  readonly dev?: boolean;
  /**
   * A component whose `init` or view throws (ADR 0024): by default the page goes on with that
   * component's error view (or an empty host the browser starts fresh) and the `GyralError` is
   * logged with `console.error`. A function hears each failure instead (logging, monitoring).
   * `'throw'` ends the render with the failure instead; `renderPage` then renders the whole page
   * first, so it throws before any byte is sent and the route can answer with an error page.
   */
  readonly onError?: ((error: GyralError) => void) | 'throw';
  /**
   * Automatic component loading: the page links the client modules of exactly the components
   * it rendered (their preload links and the loader), after the body, and nothing when it
   * rendered none. `productionServer` and `gyralDevServer` hand it to `createApp`.
   */
  readonly components?: ComponentAssets;
}
```


## `@gyral/ssr/static`

### Functions

| Name | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`assetHandler`](#ssr-static-assethandler) | Serves content-hashed files from `dir` at `prefix` (`/assets/` by default) for GET and HEAD, with `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `content-type` by extension, `content-length` and `x-content-type-options: nosniff`. |
| [`clientAssetsFromManifest`](#ssr-static-clientassetsfrommanifest) | `ClientAssets` for `entry`, read from a Vite build manifest (`build.manifest: true`). |
| [`componentsFromManifest`](#ssr-static-componentsfrommanifest) | `componentAssets` read from a client build directory (`dist/client`): its `.vite/manifest.json` and the preset's `.vite/gyral-components.json`. |
| [`prerender`](#ssr-static-prerender) | Renders each path through the app (exactly what a request would get) and writes the HTML. |
| [`productionServer`](#ssr-static-productionserver) | A production request handler (framework-neutral: mount its `fetch` in Hono, Node, …): - `GET`/`HEAD /assets/*`: content-hashed client build output, cached immutable (`assetHandler`); - `GET`/`HEAD` of a prerendered path: the `static/` file, revalidated on every use; - everything else (other GETs, POSTs): the request-time app, `no-cache` unless it set one. |
| [`writeComponentStyleManifest`](#ssr-static-writecomponentstylemanifest) | After the client build, automatically import its discovered/listed component modules in a temporary SSR bundle and fresh Node process, then write their real `styleHashes()` as JSON. |

#### `assetHandler`

```ts
function assetHandler(options: AssetHandlerOptions): AssetHandler
```

Serves content-hashed files from `dir` at `prefix` (`/assets/` by default) for GET and HEAD,
with `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, `content-type` by extension,
`content-length` and `x-content-type-options: nosniff`. Paths that are not under `dir` after
decoding (`..`, encoded slashes leading out) or have a dot segment (`.hidden`) are refused;
a malformed escape is a 400. Misses are 404 with `cache-control: no-store`, so a CDN never
keeps a miss for a file the next deploy brings. Other methods get 405. A single-range
`Range` request gets a 206 with that slice (media seeking: Safari won't play video without
it); several ranges get the whole file. Hashed files never change, so `If-Range` isn't needed.

#### `clientAssetsFromManifest`

```ts
async function clientAssetsFromManifest(
  manifestPath: string,
  entry: string,
  also: readonly string[] = [],
  options: ManifestOptions = {},
): Promise<ClientAssets>
```

`ClientAssets` for `entry`, read from a Vite build manifest (`build.manifest: true`). `also`:
manifest keys of modules the page will import lazily (a route's module, by source path such
as `src/routes/product.ts`), preloaded too, each with its static imports and CSS.
`options.base`: Vite's `base`, which every URL starts with.

#### `componentsFromManifest`

```ts
async function componentsFromManifest(
  clientDir: string,
  options: ManifestOptions = {},
): Promise<ComponentAssets | undefined>
```

`componentAssets` read from a client build directory (`dist/client`): its
`.vite/manifest.json` and the preset's `.vite/gyral-components.json`. Undefined when the
build wasn't made with `components: true`.

#### `prerender`

```ts
async function prerender(options: PrerenderOptions): Promise<readonly PrerenderedPage[]>
```

Renders each path through the app (exactly what a request would get) and writes the HTML.
A non-200 response fails the build: an `ssg` route must render successfully.

#### `productionServer`

```ts
async function productionServer<Env = unknown>(
  options: ProductionOptions<Env>,
): Promise<FetchApp<Env>>
```

A production request handler (framework-neutral: mount its `fetch` in Hono, Node, …):
- `GET`/`HEAD /assets/*`: content-hashed client build output, cached immutable
  (`assetHandler`);
- `GET`/`HEAD` of a prerendered path: the `static/` file, revalidated on every use;
- everything else (other GETs, POSTs): the request-time app, `no-cache` unless it set one.

Its `fetch` passes the server's `env` (`toNodeListener`'s `{ incoming, remoteAddress }`) on to
the app, so the app can read the client's address.

#### `writeComponentStyleManifest`

```ts
async function writeComponentStyleManifest(
  options: ComponentStyleManifestOptions,
): Promise<ComponentStyleManifest>
```

After the client build, automatically import its discovered/listed component modules in a
temporary SSR bundle and fresh Node process, then write their real `styleHashes()` as JSON.
This executes trusted application module initialization at BUILD time: modules must be
SSR-safe. It is not AST guessing and must not run against untrusted source. Vite is loaded
only when invoked; production reads the resulting JSON into `CspOptions.componentStyleHashes`.

### Types and interfaces

You rarely write most of these yourself: TypeScript infers them from the functions above. Look one up when an example or a compiler error names it.

| Name | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`AppAssets`](#ssr-static-appassets) | What `productionServer` hands `createApp`: the built entry and what pages link with it. |
| [`AssetHandler`](#ssr-static-assethandler) | Answers a request under the prefix, `undefined` for any other path. |
| [`AssetHandlerOptions`](#ssr-static-assethandleroptions) |  |
| [`ClientAssets`](#ssr-static-clientassets) | What a server-rendered page loads: the client entry, the modules to preload, the CSS. |
| [`ComponentStyleManifest`](#ssr-static-componentstylemanifest) |  |
| [`ComponentStyleManifestOptions`](#ssr-static-componentstylemanifestoptions) |  |
| [`FetchApp`](#ssr-static-fetchapp) | Anything with a fetch handler: a Hono app, or a plain function. |
| [`ManifestChunk`](#ssr-static-manifestchunk) | One chunk of Vite's `.vite/manifest.json` (the fields serving uses). |
| [`ManifestOptions`](#ssr-static-manifestoptions) | Where the build is served: Vite's `base` (default `/`), which the manifest's paths omit. |
| [`PageAssets`](#ssr-static-pageassets) | The page-level parts of `ClientAssets`, named as `renderPage` takes them. |
| [`PrerenderedPage`](#ssr-static-prerenderedpage) |  |
| [`PrerenderOptions`](#ssr-static-prerenderoptions) |  |
| [`ProductionOptions`](#ssr-static-productionoptions) |  |
| [`RenderMode`](#ssr-static-rendermode) | How a route is rendered. |
| [`ViteManifest`](#ssr-static-vitemanifest) | Vite's build manifest (`build.manifest: true`): chunks by source path or chunk key. |

#### `AppAssets`

```ts
interface AppAssets extends PageAssets {
  /** The built client entry's URL; undefined when the build has none (components only). */
  readonly clientEntry: string | undefined;
  /**
   * For `renderPage({ components })` when the build was made with
   * `gyral({ components: true })`: each page links exactly the components it rendered.
   */
  readonly components: ComponentAssets | undefined;
  /** `modulepreload` and `stylesheets` with `modules` added (cached per list). */
  readonly assets: (modules: readonly string[]) => PageAssets;
  /** `assets(modules).modulepreload`. */
  readonly preload: (modules: readonly string[]) => readonly string[];
}
```

What `productionServer` hands `createApp`: the built entry and what pages link with it.

#### `AssetHandler`

```ts
type AssetHandler = (request: Request) => Promise<Response | undefined>;
```

Answers a request under the prefix, `undefined` for any other path. Never throws.

#### `AssetHandlerOptions`

```ts
interface AssetHandlerOptions {
  /** The directory served under `prefix`, e.g. `dist/client/assets`. */
  readonly dir: string;
  /** The URL path prefix, with both slashes. Default `/assets/`. */
  readonly prefix?: string;
  /**
   * Keep served files in memory (hashed files never change): `true` (default) up to 64 MiB,
   * `{ maxBytes }` for another bound (least recently served files are dropped first), `false`
   * to read every request from disk. Misses are never cached.
   */
  readonly cache?: boolean | { readonly maxBytes: number };
}
```


#### `ClientAssets`

```ts
interface ClientAssets {
  /** The entry chunk's URL, for `renderPage({ scripts })`. */
  readonly entry: string;
  /**
   * Chunks the entry is known to need, for `renderPage({ modulepreload })`: the entry itself first
   * (when there is anything else), then its static imports and Gyral's lazily loaded hydration
   * chunk with its imports. Without the hints the browser
   * finds them only after it has fetched and parsed the entry (a server-rendered page would
   * fetch the hydration chunk a round trip later still).
   */
  readonly modulepreload: readonly string[];
  /**
   * The hashed CSS files of those chunks, for `renderPage({ stylesheets })`: what Vite emitted for
   * CSS imported by the entry, its static imports and the `also` modules, each chunk's after
   * its imports' (module order), each file once.
   */
  readonly css: readonly string[];
}
```

What a server-rendered page loads: the client entry, the modules to preload, the CSS.

#### `ComponentStyleManifest`

```ts
interface ComponentStyleManifest {
  readonly schema: 1;
  /** Sorted, deduplicated, quoted CSP SHA-256 sources for actual serialized shadow styles. */
  readonly hashes: readonly string[];
}
```


#### `ComponentStyleManifestOptions`

```ts
interface ComponentStyleManifestOptions {
  /** Application root used by its client build. Its component modules must be SSR-safe. */
  readonly root: string;
  /** Client output from `gyral({ components: true })`, including `.vite` metadata. */
  readonly clientDir: string;
  /** Standalone JSON deployment artifact; no component module is needed to read it later. */
  readonly outFile: string;
  /** Build-time aliases/plugins used by application modules. No config file is loaded. */
  readonly vite?: InlineConfig;
}
```


#### `FetchApp`

```ts
interface FetchApp<Env = unknown> {
  readonly fetch: (request: Request, env?: Env) => Response | Promise<Response>;
}
```

Anything with a fetch handler: a Hono app, or a plain function. `env` is what the server
passes along (`toNodeListener`'s `{ incoming, remoteAddress }`); a prerender passes none.

#### `ManifestChunk`

```ts
interface ManifestChunk {
  readonly file: string;
  readonly imports?: readonly string[];
  readonly dynamicImports?: readonly string[];
  readonly css?: readonly string[];
}
```

One chunk of Vite's `.vite/manifest.json` (the fields serving uses).

#### `ManifestOptions`

```ts
interface ManifestOptions {
  /** Vite's `base`, e.g. `/app/` (a missing trailing slash is added). Default `/`. */
  readonly base?: string;
}
```

Where the build is served: Vite's `base` (default `/`), which the manifest's paths omit.

#### `PageAssets`

```ts
interface PageAssets {
  readonly modulepreload: readonly string[];
  readonly stylesheets: readonly string[];
}
```

The page-level parts of `ClientAssets`, named as `renderPage` takes them.

#### `PrerenderedPage`

```ts
interface PrerenderedPage {
  readonly path: string;
  readonly file: string;
  readonly status: number;
}
```


#### `PrerenderOptions`

```ts
interface PrerenderOptions {
  readonly app: FetchApp;
  /** URL paths to render, e.g. every `ssg` route of the route table. */
  readonly paths: readonly string[];
  /** Directory the HTML files go to (`/about` → `<outDir>/about/index.html`). */
  readonly outDir: string;
  /** Origin used for the requests (absolute URLs in canonical links etc.). */
  readonly origin?: string;
}
```


#### `ProductionOptions`

```ts
interface ProductionOptions<Env = unknown> {
  /** Build output: `client/` (Vite, with `.vite/manifest.json`) and `static/` (prerendered). */
  readonly distDir: string;
  /**
   * The client entry as named in the Vite manifest. Default `src/entry-client.ts`. A build made
   * with `gyral({ components: true })` may have none: pages then load components
   * through `components` alone.
   */
  readonly entry?: string;
  /**
   * The directory served at `/assets/`. Default `<distDir>/client/assets`; point it at a
   * directory that keeps older releases' hashed files too, so tabs opened before a deploy keep
   * loading their chunks.
   */
  readonly assetsDir?: string;
  /**
   * Prerendered pages. Default `<distDir>/static`; `false` when the app prerenders nothing, so
   * page requests don't look for files first.
   */
  readonly staticDir?: string | false;
  /**
   * Vite's `base` when the build is served under a path (e.g. `/app/`): the entry, preload and
   * stylesheet URLs start with it, and assets are served at `<base>assets/`. Default `/`.
   */
  readonly base?: string;
  /** Keep served assets in memory (`assetHandler`'s `cache`). Default `true`. */
  readonly cache?: boolean | { readonly maxBytes: number };
  /**
   * Builds the request-time renderer (the same app the prerender step used). Pass
   * `modulepreload` and `stylesheets` on to `renderPage` so pages preload what the entry needs
   * and link its hashed CSS. A page that imports modules lazily (a route's chunk) spreads
   * `assets(modules)` instead: both lists plus those modules, their imports and their CSS
   * (`clientAssetsFromManifest`' `also`). `preload(modules)` is `assets(modules).modulepreload`.
   */
  readonly createApp: (options: AppAssets) => FetchApp<Env>;
  /**
   * Sees every response before it goes out (built assets, prerendered pages and the app's), to
   * add headers such as a CSP or security headers, or cookies. Return the response to send.
   */
  readonly onResponse?: (response: Response, request: Request) => Response | Promise<Response>;
}
```


#### `RenderMode`

```ts
type RenderMode = 'ssg' | 'ssr' | 'csr';
```

How a route is rendered.

#### `ViteManifest`

```ts
type ViteManifest = Readonly<Record<string, ManifestChunk>>;
```

Vite's build manifest (`build.manifest: true`): chunks by source path or chunk key.

## `@gyral/ssr/node`

### Functions

| Name | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`gyralDevMiddleware`](#ssr-node-gyraldevmiddleware) | The development server of a server-rendered app, as middleware for a server of its own: |
| [`gyralDevServer`](#ssr-node-gyraldevserver) | Starts the development server of a server-rendered app: |
| [`toNodeListener`](#ssr-node-tonodelistener) | A `node:http` request listener that runs `fetch` for each request: - the `Request` gets the method, URL (on `origin`), headers and, for methods other than `GET`/`HEAD`, the body as a stream; its `signal` aborts when the client disconnects; - the `Response` body is piped with backpressure (a slow client pauses the stream, so a `renderPage` body renders as fast as it is read) and cancelled on disconnect; - `HEAD` sends the headers only; each `set-cookie` stays its own header; - an unparsable request target is a 400; a throwing handler a 500 (`onError` sees it); - the handler's second argument is a {@link NodeEnv}: `{ incoming, remoteAddress }`. |

#### `gyralDevMiddleware`

```ts
async function gyralDevMiddleware<M, S = undefined>(
  options: DevMiddlewareOptions<M, S>,
): Promise<DevMiddleware>
```

The development server of a server-rendered app, as middleware for a server of its own:


```ts
const dev = await gyralDevMiddleware({ entry: '/server/app.ts', app: (mod) => mod.app });
express().use('/api', api).use(dev.middleware).listen(5173);
```

Client modules, CSS and HMR come from Vite (middleware mode); any other request renders
through the app, streamed. A render error answers 500 with Vite's error overlay.

#### `gyralDevServer`

```ts
async function gyralDevServer<M, S = undefined>(
  options: DevServerOptions<M, S>,
): Promise<DevServer>
```

Starts the development server of a server-rendered app:


```ts
await gyralDevServer({
  entry: '/server/app.ts',
  app: (mod: typeof import('./app.js'), { components }) => mod.createApp({ components }),
});
```

`gyralDevMiddleware` on its own HTTP server.

#### `toNodeListener`

```ts
function toNodeListener(
  fetch: FetchHandler,
  options: NodeListenerOptions = {},
): NodeListener
```

A `node:http` request listener that runs `fetch` for each request:
- the `Request` gets the method, URL (on `origin`), headers and, for methods other than
  `GET`/`HEAD`, the body as a stream; its `signal` aborts when the client disconnects;
- the `Response` body is piped with backpressure (a slow client pauses the stream, so a
  `renderPage` body renders as fast as it is read) and cancelled on disconnect;
- `HEAD` sends the headers only; each `set-cookie` stays its own header;
- an unparsable request target is a 400; a throwing handler a 500 (`onError` sees it);
- the handler's second argument is a {@link NodeEnv}: `{ incoming, remoteAddress }`.

### Types and interfaces

You rarely write most of these yourself: TypeScript infers them from the functions above. Look one up when an example or a compiler error names it.

| Name | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`DevApp`](#ssr-node-devapp) | A request handler: a Hono app, `productionServer`'s result, or `{ fetch }`. |
| [`DevMiddleware`](#ssr-node-devmiddleware) |  |
| [`DevMiddlewareOptions`](#ssr-node-devmiddlewareoptions) |  |
| [`DevServer`](#ssr-node-devserver) |  |
| [`DevServerContext`](#ssr-node-devservercontext) | What `gyralDevServer` hands the app factory with each freshly loaded module. |
| [`DevServerOptions`](#ssr-node-devserveroptions) |  |
| [`FetchHandler`](#ssr-node-fetchhandler) | A fetch handler: `productionServer(…).fetch`, a Hono app's `fetch`, or a plain function. |
| [`NodeEnv`](#ssr-node-nodeenv) | What `toNodeListener` passes as the handler's second argument: the Node request and the client's address. |
| [`NodeListener`](#ssr-node-nodelistener) | A Node `request` listener: `createServer(toNodeListener(app.fetch))`. |
| [`NodeListenerOptions`](#ssr-node-nodelisteneroptions) |  |

#### `DevApp`

```ts
interface DevApp {
  readonly fetch: (request: Request, env: NodeEnv) => Response | Promise<Response>;
}
```

A request handler: a Hono app, `productionServer`'s result, or `{ fetch }`.

#### `DevMiddleware`

```ts
interface DevMiddleware {
  /**
   * A Connect-style handler: Express and Connect take it with `app.use()`, Fastify through
   * `@fastify/middie`. It answers every request that reaches it (Vite's modules, then the app),
   * so mount the server's own routes before it.
   */
  readonly middleware: (req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse) => void;
  readonly vite: ViteDevServer;
  /** Stops Vite. */
  readonly close: () => Promise<void>;
}
```


#### `DevMiddlewareOptions`

```ts
interface DevMiddlewareOptions<M, S> {
  /** The server module, from Vite's root (e.g. `/server/app.ts`). Vite reloads it after an edit. */
  readonly entry: string;
  /**
   * Builds the request handler from the module just loaded: once per module version (Vite gives
   * a new module after an edit) and set of components, not per request. Keep per-request work
   * in the handler.
   */
  readonly app: (module: M, context: DevServerContext<S>) => DevApp;
  /**
   * State that must outlive module reloads (an in-memory database, say): created once, from the
   * first module loaded, and passed to every `app` call.
   */
  readonly state?: (module: M) => S;
  /** The HMR WebSocket's port, so several dev servers can run side by side. Default Vite's. */
  readonly hmrPort?: number;
  /** `toNodeListener`'s `origin`: the public origin when absolute URLs matter. */
  readonly origin?: string;
  /** More Vite settings (root, configFile, plugins, …), merged under the server settings. */
  readonly vite?: InlineConfig;
}
```


#### `DevServer`

```ts
interface DevServer {
  /** `http://host:port/` the server listens on. */
  readonly url: string;
  readonly server: Server;
  readonly vite: ViteDevServer;
  /** Stops the HTTP server and Vite. */
  readonly close: () => Promise<void>;
}
```


#### `DevServerContext`

```ts
interface DevServerContext<S> {
  /**
   * For `renderPage({ components })` when the Vite config uses `gyral({ components })`:
   * the loader and the tags it knows. Undefined otherwise.
   */
  readonly components: ComponentAssets | undefined;
  /** The value `state` created once, kept across module reloads. */
  readonly state: S;
}
```

What `gyralDevServer` hands the app factory with each freshly loaded module.

#### `DevServerOptions`

```ts
interface DevServerOptions<M, S> extends DevMiddlewareOptions<M, S> {
  /** Default: the `PORT` environment variable, else 5173. `0` picks a free port. */
  readonly port?: number;
  /** Default: Node's (all interfaces). */
  readonly host?: string;
}
```


#### `FetchHandler`

```ts
type FetchHandler = (request: Request, env: NodeEnv) => Response | Promise<Response>;
```

A fetch handler: `productionServer(…).fetch`, a Hono app's `fetch`, or a plain function. Under
`toNodeListener` it also receives a {@link NodeEnv}; handlers that don't need it ignore it.

#### `NodeEnv`

```ts
interface NodeEnv {
  /** The Node request, for anything `Request` doesn't carry (socket, TLS details). */
  readonly incoming: IncomingMessage;
  /**
   * The peer's IP address (`req.socket.remoteAddress`), or `undefined` once the socket is gone.
   * Behind a proxy this is the proxy: read `X-Forwarded-For` only when the proxy is known.
   */
  readonly remoteAddress: string | undefined;
}
```

What `toNodeListener` passes as the handler's second argument: the Node request
and the client's address. `{ incoming }` is the shape Hono's Node adapter uses, so
`getConnInfo` from `@hono/node-server/conninfo` works unchanged.

#### `NodeListener`

```ts
type NodeListener = (req: IncomingMessage, res: ServerResponse) => void;
```

A Node `request` listener: `createServer(toNodeListener(app.fetch))`.

#### `NodeListenerOptions`

```ts
interface NodeListenerOptions {
  /**
   * The origin request URLs are built on, e.g. `https://example.com` behind a proxy. Default:
   * `http://` (`https://` on a TLS socket) plus the request's `Host` header, which the client
   * chooses: set it when the app writes absolute URLs (canonical links, redirects).
   */
  readonly origin?: string;
  /**
   * Called when the handler throws or the response body fails, before the 500 (or, once the
   * headers are out, before the connection is cut). Default: `console.error`.
   */
  readonly onError?: (error: unknown, request: Request) => void;
}
```

# @gyral/testing

> Gyral test helpers: pure update stepping, command helpers, fake drivers, virtual time, SSR page mounting, server rendering in Vitest browser tests.

Source: https://gyral.dev/docs/api/testing/

Gyral test helpers: pure update stepping, command helpers, fake drivers, virtual time, SSR page mounting, server rendering in Vitest browser tests.

```sh
npm install @gyral/testing @gyral/core
```

> **Writing code? Start from working code, not from this page.** [Testing](https://gyral.dev/docs/testing/). Adapt the closest example and check it, then look a name up here when you are about to call it.

Generated from the package's type declarations. Entry points: [`@gyral/testing`](#gyraltesting), [`@gyral/testing/vitest`](#gyraltestingvitest).

## `@gyral/testing`

### Functions

| Name | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`callsIn`](#testing-callsin) | The element method calls among the commands (`call(selector, method, ...args)`), in order: |
| [`collectErrors`](#testing-collecterrors) | Starts collecting every `GyralError` Gyral reports, so deliberate failures don't fail the test run. |
| [`commandsFor`](#testing-commandsfor) | The commands addressed to `driver` (matched by name, so fakes and real drivers agree). |
| [`fakeDriver`](#testing-fakedriver) | A recording driver for DOM-level tests: `el.drivers = { http: fakeDriver(http) }`. |
| [`focusTargetsIn`](#testing-focustargetsin) | The focus requests among the commands (`focus(selector, options)`), in order: |
| [`hydrated`](#testing-hydrated) | Waits until the page's Gyral components have rendered (see `settled()`): releases lazy islands if asked, then `await settled()`. |
| [`initial`](#testing-initial) | Runs `init` without a DOM. |
| [`inputsFor`](#testing-inputsfor) | The inputs of the commands addressed to `driver`; given a store, the messages the commands `send()` to it, in order (ADR 0013). |
| [`mount`](#testing-mount) | Creates `component` (a class from `define()` or a registered tag name), sets `props`, `attrs`, `drivers` and `stores`, appends it, and waits for its first render. |
| [`mountSsr`](#testing-mountssr) | Mounts server output: a full document (head + body) or a body fragment. |
| [`outputsIn`](#testing-outputsin) | The outputs the commands send to the parent component (`emit`, `outputs<O>()`), in order. |
| [`parse`](#testing-parse) | Runs the parser of intent `name` with `input` (only the fields the parser reads are needed: `{ value: '3' }`, `{ key: 'Enter' }`, `{ detail }`). |
| [`reject`](#testing-reject) | The message a command produces if its driver fails with `error` (already typed, i.e. |
| [`resetDocumentStores`](#testing-resetdocumentstores) | Tests only: forget the document default so each test starts clean. |
| [`resolve`](#testing-resolve) | The message a command produces if its driver succeeds with `output`. |
| [`run`](#testing-run) | Folds messages through `update`, collecting every command (including `init`'s). |
| [`step`](#testing-step) | Feeds one message through `update` without a DOM. |
| [`stepStore`](#testing-stepstore) | Feeds one message through a store's `update` without an instance. |
| [`subscriptionsFor`](#testing-subscriptionsfor) | The commands `spec.subscriptions` asks to keep running for `state` and `props` (ADR 0025), without a DOM: `subscriptionsFor(Clock.spec, { live: true })`. |
| [`viewOf`](#testing-viewof) | Calls a component's pure view without mounting, a DOM shim or consumer casts. |
| [`virtualTime`](#testing-virtualtime) | Replaces timers and `Date` with a virtual clock (ADR 0006, "Testing"). |

#### `callsIn`

```ts
function callsIn(commands: ReadonlyArray<Command<unknown>>): readonly CallInput[]
```

The element method calls among the commands (`call(selector, method, ...args)`), in order:


```ts
expect(callsIn(next.commands)).toEqual([{ selector: 'video', method: 'play', args: [] }]);
```


#### `collectErrors`

```ts
function collectErrors(): CollectedErrors
```

Starts collecting every `GyralError` Gyral reports, so deliberate failures don't fail the
test run. Errors that aren't Gyral's are left alone. Call `stop()` when the test ends.

#### `commandsFor`

```ts
function commandsFor<I, M>(
  commands: ReadonlyArray<Command<M>>,
  driver: Driver<I, unknown> | Named,
): ReadonlyArray<Command<M> & { readonly input: I }>
```

The commands addressed to `driver` (matched by name, so fakes and real drivers agree).

#### `fakeDriver`

```ts
function fakeDriver<I = unknown, O = unknown, E = unknown>(
  of: string | Driver<I, O, E>,
  optionsOrRun: FakeOptions<I, O, E> | FakeRun<I, O> = {},
): FakeDriver<I, O, E>
```

A recording driver for DOM-level tests: `el.drivers = { http: fakeDriver(http) }`.
Pass a real driver to copy its name and concurrency, or just a name. Failures pass
through unchanged unless you give `toError`, so `rejectNext(error)` takes the typed error.
A function as the second argument answers every call (`impl`):


```ts
el.drivers = { 'url-sync': fakeDriver<string | null, void>('url-sync', (q) => void urls.push(q)) };
```

Fakes go into `el.drivers` and `provideDrivers` as they are, with no cast.

#### `focusTargetsIn`

```ts
function focusTargetsIn(commands: ReadonlyArray<Command<unknown>>): readonly FocusTarget[]
```

The focus requests among the commands (`focus(selector, options)`), in order:


```ts
expect(focusTargetsIn(next.commands)).toEqual([{ selector: '#results' }]);
```


#### `hydrated`

```ts
async function hydrated(
  page: MountedSsr | ParentNode,
  options: HydratedOptions = {},
): Promise<void>
```

Waits until the page's Gyral components have rendered (see `settled()`): releases lazy islands if asked, then `await settled()`. Islands still
deferred are left alone. It throws when a server-rendered custom element never upgraded
(import its module, or list it in `allowUndefined`). Given a `MountedSsr`, it also throws
when console errors/warnings or uncaught errors were recorded since mounting.

#### `initial`

```ts
function initial<S, M extends Tagged, P>(
  spec: ComponentSpec<S, M, P>,
  props: P = {} as P,
): Stepped<S, M>
```

Runs `init` without a DOM. `props` defaults to `{}`.

#### `inputsFor`

```ts
function inputsFor<S, SM extends Tagged>(
  commands: ReadonlyArray<Command<unknown>>,
  store: Store<S, SM>,
): readonly SM[];
function inputsFor<I, M>(
  commands: ReadonlyArray<Command<M>>,
  driver: Driver<I, unknown> | Named,
): readonly I[];
```

The inputs of the commands addressed to `driver`; given a store, the messages the commands
`send()` to it, in order (ADR 0013).

#### `mount`

```ts
async function mount<K extends keyof HTMLElementTagNameMap>(
  tag: K,
  options?: MountOptions<HTMLElementTagNameMap[K]>,
): Promise<Mounted<HTMLElementTagNameMap[K]>>;
async function mount<E extends HTMLElement>(
  component: Constructor<E> | string,
  options?: MountOptions<E>,
): Promise<Mounted<E>>;
```

Creates `component` (a class from `define()` or a registered tag name), sets `props`,
`attrs`, `drivers` and `stores`, appends it, and waits for its first render.

#### `mountSsr`

```ts
function mountSsr(html: string, options: MountSsrOptions = {}): MountedSsr
```

Mounts server output: a full document (head + body) or a body fragment. Call it before
importing component modules so elements upgrade and hydrate like on a real page load.
- Only `<head>` styles are applied: `<style>` inside Declarative Shadow DOM belongs to its
  shadow root and must not leak into the page.
- The store seed, named `<meta>`s and the managed head are restored, as the browser would
  see them.

#### `outputsIn`

```ts
function outputsIn<C extends WithOutputs>(
  commands: ReadonlyArray<Command<unknown>>,
  component: C,
): ReadonlyArray<OutputsOf<C>>;
function outputsIn<O extends Tagged = Tagged>(
  commands: ReadonlyArray<Command<unknown>>,
): readonly O[];
```

The outputs the commands send to the parent component (`emit`, `outputs<O>()`), in order.
Pass the component class to type them by its output union (`OutputsOf<typeof Item>`):


```ts
expect(outputsIn(next.commands, Item)).toEqual([{ _tag: 'Picked', id: 1 }]);
```

The outputs, typed by the union you name: `outputsIn<Out>(commands)`.

#### `parse`

```ts
function parse<S, M extends Tagged, P, N extends string, K extends N>(
  component: SpecOf<S, M, P, N>,
  name: K,
  input: Partial<IntentInput> = {},
  options: ParseOptions<NoInfer<S>, NoInfer<P>> = {},
): Parsed<M, K> | IntentRejected | undefined | Promise<Parsed<M, K> | IntentRejected | undefined>
```

Runs the parser of intent `name` with `input` (only the fields the parser reads are needed:
`{ value: '3' }`, `{ key: 'Enter' }`, `{ detail }`). Returns what the parser returns: a
message, an `IntentRejected`, `undefined` (ignored or declined), or a promise of one.

#### `reject`

```ts
function reject<M>(command: Command<M>, error: unknown): M | undefined
```

The message a command produces if its driver fails with `error` (already typed, i.e.
after the driver's `toError`). `undefined` when the command has no `onFailure`.

#### `resetDocumentStores`

```ts
function resetDocumentStores(): void
```

Tests only: forget the document default so each test starts clean.

#### `resolve`

```ts
function resolve<M>(command: Command<M>, output: unknown): M | undefined
```

The message a command produces if its driver succeeds with `output`.

#### `run`

```ts
function run<S, M extends Tagged, P>(
  spec: ComponentSpec<S, M, P>,
  messages: ReadonlyArray<NoInfer<StepMessage<M, P>>>,
  options: NoInfer<RunOptions<S, P>> = {},
): Ran<S, M>
```

Folds messages through `update`, collecting every command (including `init`'s).

#### `step`

```ts
function step<S, M extends Tagged, P>(
  spec: ComponentSpec<S, M, P>,
  state: NoInfer<S>,
  // NoInfer: M comes from the spec, so literal messages are checked against it.
  msg: NoInfer<StepMessage<M, P>>,
  props: NoInfer<P> = {} as P,
  stores: readonly AnyStoreInstance[] = [],
): Stepped<S, M>
```

Feeds one message through `update` without a DOM. Framework messages (`PropsChanged`,
`IntentRejected`, `StoreChanged`, `Hydrated`, `Errored`) without a reducer leave state unchanged, as in
the element. `stores` are the instances `ctx.read()` sees.

#### `stepStore`

```ts
function stepStore<S, M extends Tagged>(
  store: Store<S, M>,
  state: NoInfer<S>,
  msg: NoInfer<M>,
): Stepped<S, M>
```

Feeds one message through a store's `update` without an instance.

#### `subscriptionsFor`

```ts
function subscriptionsFor<S, M extends Tagged, P>(
  spec: ComponentSpec<S, M, P>,
  state: NoInfer<S>,
  props: NoInfer<P> = {} as P,
): ReadonlyArray<Command<M>>
```

The commands `spec.subscriptions` asks to keep running for `state` and `props` (ADR 0025),
without a DOM: `subscriptionsFor(Clock.spec, { live: true })`. A spec without the field gives
none. Assert their inputs with `inputsFor`, as for any commands.

#### `viewOf`

```ts
function viewOf<S, M extends Tagged, P, N extends string>(
  component: ComponentSpec<S, M, P, N> | GyralElementClass<S, M, P, Tagged, N>,
  state: NoInfer<S>,
  options: ViewOptions<NoInfer<P>> = {},
): ChildValue
```

Calls a component's pure view without mounting, a DOM shim or consumer casts. Use
`renderToString(viewOf(Component, state, { props, stores }), { dev: false })` for stable
HTML assertions. Hooks, native validity, focus and hydration need real-browser tests.

#### `virtualTime`

```ts
function virtualTime(): VirtualTime
```

Replaces timers and `Date` with a virtual clock (ADR 0006, "Testing"). It patches the
platform rather than Gyral's runtime, so it covers drivers, debounces and retry delays
alike and does not depend on how the interpreter is implemented. Microtasks stay real,
so promises and the runtime keep working. Animation frames are faked only where they exist,
so model and driver tests can use it in a Node project.

#### `CollectedErrors`

```ts
interface CollectedErrors {
  readonly errors: readonly GyralError[];
  /** Stops collecting; later failures are reported as usual. */
  stop(): void;
}
```

The failures collected so far; `stop()` removes the listeners.

#### `FakeCall`

```ts
interface FakeCall<I, O> {
  readonly input: I;
  readonly signal: AbortSignal;
  /** Settles this call (only for fakes without `impl`). */
  readonly resolve: (output: O) => void;
  readonly reject: (error: unknown) => void;
  /** Streams a value into this call (DriverContext.emit); ignored once settled or aborted. */
  readonly emit: (output: O) => void;
  readonly settled: boolean;
}
```

One recorded `run` of a fake driver.

#### `FakeDriver`

```ts
interface FakeDriver<I, O, E> extends Driver<I, O, E> {
  readonly calls: ReadonlyArray<FakeCall<I, O>>;
  /** Inputs of every call so far. */
  readonly inputs: readonly I[];
  /** Settles the oldest unsettled, non-aborted call. Throws if there is none. */
  resolveNext(output: O): void;
  rejectNext(error: unknown): void;
  /** Streams a value into the newest call that is still running. Throws if there is none. */
  emitNext(output: O): void;
}
```


#### `FakeOptions`

```ts
interface FakeOptions<I, O, E> {
  /** Answer calls immediately. Without it, calls wait for `resolveNext`/`rejectNext`. */
  readonly impl?: FakeRun<I, O>;
  readonly concurrency?: Concurrency;
  readonly toError?: (cause: unknown) => E;
}
```


#### `FakeRun`

```ts
type FakeRun<I, O> = (input: I, ctx: DriverContext<O>) => O | Promise<O>;
```

What a fake answers each call with (`FakeOptions.impl`).

#### `FocusTarget`

```ts
interface FocusTarget extends FocusOptions {
  readonly selector: string;
}
```

What a `focus()` command asks for: the selector and its options.

#### `HydratedOptions`

```ts
interface HydratedOptions {
  /**
   * Custom element tags allowed to stay undefined (never upgraded). `gyral-stores` is always
   * allowed: in the browser it is a plain scoping element.
   */
  readonly allowUndefined?: readonly string[];
  /**
   * Release every lazy island first (`defer-hydration` + `data-gyral-hydrate`), as if each
   * one's trigger had fired. Default `false`: islands keep waiting.
   */
  readonly releaseIslands?: boolean;
}
```


#### `Mounted`

```ts
interface Mounted<E extends HTMLElement> {
  readonly el: E;
  /** The first match in the element's shadow root (or light DOM), or null. */
  $(selector: string): HTMLElement | null;
  /** Every match in the element's shadow root (or light DOM). */
  $$(selector: string): HTMLElement[];
  /** Sets a control's value as typing would, fires `input` and `change`, then waits. */
  type(selector: string, text: string): Promise<void>;
  /** Clicks the first match, then waits. */
  click(selector: string): Promise<void>;
  /** Waits until rendering, commands and messages have settled (`settled()`). */
  settled(): Promise<void>;
  /** Removes the element (and its overrides with it). */
  dispose(): void;
}
```


#### `MountedSsr`

```ts
interface MountedSsr {
  /** The element holding the server body (Declarative Shadow DOM already parsed). */
  readonly root: HTMLElement;
  /** Console errors/warnings and uncaught errors seen since mounting (see `hydrated`). */
  readonly problems: readonly string[];
  readonly unmount: () => void;
}
```


#### `MountOptions`

```ts
interface MountOptions<E extends HTMLElement> {
  /** Props, set as properties before the element connects. */
  readonly props?: PropsOf<E> & Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
  /** Attributes, set before the element connects. */
  readonly attrs?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  /** Driver substitutions by name (`el.drivers`), set before the element connects. */
  readonly drivers?: DriverOverrides | DriverList;
  /** Store instances by name (`el.stores`), set before the element connects. */
  readonly stores?: StoreOverrides;
  /** Query the element's light DOM instead of its shadow root (for `shadow: false`). */
  readonly light?: boolean;
  /** Where to append the element. Default `document.body`. */
  readonly parent?: ParentNode;
}
```


#### `MountSsrOptions`

```ts
interface MountSsrOptions {
  /** Restore the page-level store seed (`data-gyral-stores`). Default `true`. */
  readonly stores?: boolean;
  /** Copy `<meta name=…>` elements from the head (e.g. a CSRF token). Default `true`. */
  readonly metas?: boolean;
  /**
   * Copy the managed head (ADR 0019: elements marked `data-gyral-head`) right after the
   * document's `<title>`, as the server wrote it, so a test can check that the client's first
   * `setHead()` adopts it without writing. Default `true`.
   */
  readonly head?: boolean;
}
```


#### `ParseOptions`

```ts
interface ParseOptions<S, P> {
  /** Props as the component sees them. Default `{}`. */
  readonly props?: P;
  /** The state when the event fires. Default: the component's initial state for `props`. */
  readonly state?: S;
  /** Store instances `ctx.read` resolves (ADR 0013). */
  readonly stores?: readonly AnyStoreInstance[];
}
```

What `parse` passes the parser besides the input.

#### `Ran`

```ts
interface Ran<S, M> extends Stepped<S, M> {
  /** State after each message, in order. */
  readonly states: readonly S[];
}
```


#### `RunOptions`

```ts
interface RunOptions<S, P> {
  readonly props?: P;
  /** Store instances `ctx.read()` sees. */
  readonly stores?: readonly AnyStoreInstance[];
  /** Start from this state instead of `init(props)` (whose commands are then skipped). */
  readonly state?: S;
}
```


#### `StepMessage`

```ts
type StepMessage<M, P> =
  M | PropsChanged<P> | IntentRejected | StoreChanged | Hydrated | Errored;
```

#### `Stepped`

```ts
interface Stepped<S, M> {

```

A reducer result, normalised: the new state plus the commands it asked for.

#### `VirtualTime`

```ts
interface VirtualTime {
  /** Advances the clock, running due timers and the promise work between them. */
  advance(ms: number): Promise<void>;
  /** Runs every pending timer (and timers they schedule) until none remain. */
  runAll(): Promise<void>;
  /** Current virtual time in ms (`Date.now()` while installed). */
  now(): number;
  restore(): void;
}
```

Controls time in a test. Always `restore()` (for example in `afterEach`).

#### `ServerRenderRequest`

```ts
interface ServerRenderRequest {
  /**
   * The module to load on the server: relative to the test file (`'../src/counter.ts'`), an
   * absolute path, a path from the project root (`'/src/app.ts'`) or a package specifier.
   */
  readonly module: string;
  /**
   * The export to render (default `'default'`):
   * - a `define()` class: renders its element, with `props` set as properties;
   * - a function: called with `props`; it may return (or resolve to) a template result, an
   *   HTML string or a `Response` (a full page from `@gyral/ssr`'s `renderPage`, an app's
   *   `fetch` handler…);
   * - a template result: rendered as is.
   */
  readonly export?: string;
  /** Props for a component class, or the argument of a function export. */
  readonly props?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
  /**
   * Development markers and checks (`render`'s `dev` option). Default: the build of core the
   * server loads (development in Vitest).
   */
  readonly dev?: boolean;
}
```

What `renderOnServer` renders. Everything is sent from the browser, so it must be JSON.
